title: First cohomology exact sequence for surface modifications
statement: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a commutative Noetherian normal local domain of dimension $2$ [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-normal-ring, def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Put $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $f:X\to S$ and $f\circ g:X^{\prime}\to S$ be proper morphisms from integral schemes, inducing isomorphisms of function fields [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-pc-integral-scheme, def-sc-function-field], and assume $X$ is normal (all its local rings are normal domains). For cohomology and higher direct images of structure sheaves on the Zariski topology [pqf-def-cohomology], there is a short exact sequence of $A$-modules $$0\to H^1(X,\mathcal O_X)\to H^1(X^{\prime},\mathcal O_{X^{\prime}})\to H^0(X,R^1g_*\mathcal O_{X^{\prime}})\to0.$$ The sheaf $R^1g_*\mathcal O_{X^{\prime}}$ is generated by its global sections, meaning that the germs of global sections generate every stalk as an $\mathcal O_X$-module. Its support is contained in a finite set of closed points of $X$.

mathlib_searches.query: For proper birational maps of normal surfaces over a two dimensional normal local ring, H1 of structure sheaves fits into an exact sequence with H0 of R1 direct image
For surface modifications the Leray spectral sequence gives a short exact sequence of first structure sheaf cohomology and global sections of the first higher direct image
Coherent first higher direct image of a birational modification of a surface has zero dimensional support and is generated by global sections
